driver_settings.color_correction: No Color Adjustment (More Options > Color Correction > Custom > Advanced) - confirmed present and selected 2026-07-27
driver_settings.recorded: 2026-07-27 - locked in; exposure strip and blocker grid printed at these settings

exposure.uv_wavelength_nm: 390-400 (from the lamp's own marking, read 2026-08-09). Recorded as the stated range rather than collapsed to 395, because that is what is actually known. Cyanotype absorbs more strongly nearer 365, so this lamp does less work per watt - consistent with an SPE of 13:30 at 350mm. A replacement lamp at a different wavelength invalidates spe_seconds.
exposure.spe_note: read by eye from the 8-zone strip, dry: zones 6, 7 and 8 matched, zone 5 (9:30) still lighter, so the plateau begins at zone 6 = 13:30
exposure.warmup_note: Decided 2026-08-10: no warm-up. The strip that gave spe_seconds was shot cold, so 13:30 stands as measured. A UV LED reaches near-full output in seconds, and the one print that appears to have had a warm-up lost 0.13 of density range - paper white L* 96.1 against 99.8, shadows unchanged, which is what extra dose does once the shadows are already at Dmax.

measurements.note: Both halves off ONE coated sheet, so blocker and curve share a coating pass, exposure, wash and drying; they agree on density range to 0.052 log units where separate sheets disagreed by 0.19. Derived from the Photoshop-converted sRGB scans; the raw-linear route independently gave the same blocker and a curve differing by a mean of 0.005, so the colour-space handling is corroborated rather than assumed.
measurements.paper_note: Recorded 2026-08-09. Everything measured here - blocker, curve, density range, SPE - was measured on this paper and this film batch. A different paper or batch needs its own profile, not an edit of this one.
measurements.patch_colour_note: Patch rgb added 2026-08-10 by re-reading the same wedge scan; lightness unchanged. The soft proof interpolates these directly, so the print's colour is measured rather than modelled - a linear blend between paper and Prussian blue reads far too neutral through the midtones.

scan_settings.auto_corrections: all off - auto exposure/tone/backlight rescale each sheet independently
scan_settings.software: SilverFast 9.2.9 raw, converted to sRGB in Photoshop
scan_settings.note: Scan SilverFast raw then convert to sRGB before analysis. Raw output is linear despite the embedded scanner profile advertising a 2.2 TRC; analysing the raw file needs space=linear, and the converted file needs no override. Both routes agree: the derived curves differ by a mean of 0.005 and both give hue 15 deg / sat 1.0.
